scope_note: V-FINAL adversarial audit of the shipping bytes of batches/batch19/candidates/las-b19-002.json (LÄS debatt short, family badbrygga-avgift-debatt-short, title ”Vässlingsbadet och Stångklippan”, 2 questions, keys D/A) after fleet-repair-1, which rebuilt q1 option C to clear the G-STEM round-1 C-in-D containment defect and the stance leak, and applied five G-SPRÅK edits to the passage plus two to the rationales. Prime directive was to REFUTE: to make the rebuilt q1-C (”Förslaget bör genomföras som det ligger, eftersom badgästerna har nytta av utrustningen”) defensible against the passage; to break A and B; to rule on whether the q2 rounding step (31 % betald ⇒ ”sju av tio obetalda”, i.e. 69 % against 70 %) is exam-fair; to falsify the declared blind floors (q1 1-in-2, q2 1-in-3); to falsify the repair_log and the NOTES against the bytes; and to RE-RUN law 16 rather than re-read it. The keys did not fall. C, A and B are each refutable from the passage alone, and the rebuilt C is a materially better distractor than the one it replaced. What did fall: the q2 declared floor NUMBER, the q1 declared floor DERIVATION, one repair_log characterisation of the new option C, one G-REGISTER surname-distance justification, six sections of the NOTES that were never propagated after the repair, and — the audit's main new residue — an intra-bank toponym near-duplicate that no gate could see because the excluded-toponym registry is incomplete: the shipped batch15 debatt short las-b15-002 already runs on the invented municipality ”Vässlinge”, one letter from this unit's ”Vässlingen” and the stem of its ”Vässlingsbadet”, in the same lane.

A ship-blocker is expressed as verdict REFUTED, never as a custom severity (vfinal_fold.py folds any severity outside {minor, note, info} to REFUTED, fail-closed). Nothing found here rises to REFUTED: both keys are correct and uniquely text-licensed, both survive an argue-every-option re-derivation, all six mech gates re-run pass on the shipping bytes with exit 0, all 20 rationale anchor strings resolve verbatim to the passage, all 8 repair_log old→new pairs are byte-exact, the arithmetic reconciles, the three derived sheets are exact leak-free projections, and law 16 reproduces clean on four indexes with passing positive controls. The findings are one falsified floor number, one falsified floor derivation, one falsified repair_log claim, one intra-bank naming near-duplicate, one carried 3-of-3 unanimous G-SPRÅK minor on a student-facing string, two unrecorded rationale minors, six stale NOTES sections, one falsified gate justification, three law-16 coverage gaps closed, and four process/registry items.

cold_solve.method_honesty: DISCLOSED LIMIT. The tasking required reading the candidate in FULL first — keys, rationales and repair_log included — so no genuinely key-blind first solve was available to this audit. Two separate exercises are recorded below and kept strictly apart: (1) a PASSAGE RE-DERIVATION in which every option was argued FOR to a textual verdict before any option was rejected, and (2) a BLIND RECONSTRUCTION performed against stems/las-b19-002.json alone (verified to carry only candidate_id, section and the two questions — no passage, no title, no key, no rationale, no generator_meta), asking only where form and cross-question structure carry a solver. Only the second bears on the floors, and it is stated as a reconstruction, not as a virgin solve.

passage_rederivation.q1: D. Argued FOR C (”Förslaget bör genomföras som det ligger, eftersom badgästerna har nytta av utrustningen”), tested hardest as instructed, because it is the repair's new byte and the set's only pro-proposal position. C has four real footholds, all in the author's own voice: (i) ¶1 says she voted for it and calls it ”en rimlig ordning”; (ii) ¶1 states the benefit principle outright, ”pengarna oavkortat till livräddningsutrustning”; (iii) ¶2 concedes the need flat, ”Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga”; (iv) ¶3's numbers actually close — 4 800 bad × 20 kr = 96 000 kr against 61 000 kr of equipment plus 9 000 kr a year, a first-year surplus of 26 000 kr — so a solver who stops at ¶3 sees a funded proposal whose beneficiaries are the payers. That is the strongest case available and it fails four times over. (1) The frame is a retraction and says so: ”Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst, och de som läste yttrandet har rätt att veta varför.” Every pro-proposal sentence in ¶1 is explicitly marked as her FORMER view and undercut inside the same paragraph (”vilket borde ha gjort mig misstänksam mot min egen entusiasm”). (2) The revenue premise is attacked, not endorsed: ¶4's 31 % precedent plus ”Vid bryggan finns varken bom, vakt eller registreringsskylt att fotografera av, och drivkrafterna att betala blir därför ännu svagare” — the 96 000 kr is exactly what the text says will not arrive. (3) C's own stated REASON is refuted head-on, which is the best-built feature of the rebuilt option: the benefit principle is killed on geography in ”Då bekostas utrustningen av dem som badar där det sällan händer något, medan den plats där olyckorna faktiskt inträffar lämnas orörd.” C therefore fails as a whole proposition, not merely on its main clause. (4) The explicit counter-prescription names a different route: ”Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten.” C is defensible-LOOKING and decisively refutable — the repair did its job. Argued FOR A (”Avgiften kan godtas, men den bör sättas högre än förslaget anger”): the text scrutinises the fee's revenue at length, so a reader can mistake the numeric attack for an objection to the LEVEL. REJECTED, and more cleanly than the gate history records: the passage's own arithmetic shows a SURPLUS at 20 kr (96 000 vs 61 000 + 9 000), so ”too low” has no textual purchase at all; and a higher fee would strengthen the very displacement to Stångklippan the text warns of. Argued FOR B (”Den utrustning som finns räcker om skötseln förbättras”): two of the three named defects really are upkeep failures — a cut line and a ladder that ends half a metre above the water. REJECTED on three grounds: the defibrillator is not an upkeep matter but an ABSENCE (”Närmaste hjärtstartare sitter i entrén till livsmedelsbutiken, 2,3 kilometer bort”); the demand is for purchases (”två bojar med kastlina, en ny stege och en hjärtstartare i värmeskåp”, ”Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren”); and a wholly new kastlina is demanded at Stångklippan, ”där ingen räddningsutrustning finns”. D is the only option the passage licenses, and both of its halves are explicit: ”Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga” and ”Köp … över driftsbudgeten”. Containment re-checked on the repaired set: all four options are pairwise contraries; none is an instance of another.
passage_rederivation.q2: A. The planted sentence is ”Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna”. Argued FOR B (”Betalningsviljan visade sig svår att mäta”), the strongest residual, and with a wedge the gate legs did not use: betalningsGRAD (payment rate) is not betalningsVILJA (willingness to pay), so one could claim the text measured the former and never the latter. REJECTED: B does not assert that willingness went unmeasured, it asserts it ”visade sig svår att mäta”, and the text reports a completed follow-up landing on a definite figure with no note of difficulty anywhere. Argued FOR D (”Skylten togs ned efter en säsong”): ”skylt” occurs three times in the passage, so the sentence feels familiar. REJECTED: the arrangement is described in the present tense as still standing (”en skylt, en kod och tilliten till att gästen skannar”, ”en grind som står öppen hela säsongen”), and removal is never mentioned. Argued FOR C (”Nästan alla nätter blev betalda”): right quantity, wrong pole — inverts 31 % into ~90 %+. REJECTED on the figure. A is the only option on the correct pole with the correct magnitude; see q2_rounding_ruling for the 69/70 step.
passage_rederivation.agrees_with_gkey_legs: Yes, and with every leg on record: four G-KEY legs across two rounds (verdicts-gkey-1/-2 pre-repair, verdicts-gkey-r2-1/-r2-2 post-repair, folded in verdicts-gkey-resolved and verdicts-gkey-r2-resolved) all return D and A, 0 kills, 0 flags. Round attribution verified from the bytes of the justifications themselves: the r1 legs quote the PRE-repair ”Nu vill jag ta tillbaka rösten”, the r2 legs quote the POST-repair ”Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst” and address the new C, so the two post-repair legs are genuinely on the shipping bytes. G-DISTRACTOR passed both rounds on both questions.

blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.input: stems/las-b19-002.json — two prompts and eight option strings. Verified programmatically to carry no passage, no title, no key, no rationale and no generator_meta.
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.q1_lands_on: D for a form-sensitive solver; genuinely open between two for a plain one.
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.q1_path: Two strips. (1) B falls to SCOPE alone — the stem asks what the author thinks about the fee proposal and B states no view on the fee at all, being the only option that never names avgift or förslag. G-STEM r2 records exactly this at minor. (2) Shape: A (”kan godtas, men …”) and D (”Utrustningen behövs, men …”) are the two concessive two-part options; C (”bör genomföras … eftersom …”) is causal and B is conditional. A stance question on a signed opinion column conventionally keys to a concessive landing, so the form-favoured field is {A, D} — 1-in-2. Inside that pair, ”accept the fee but charge MORE” is a rare editorial landing while ”need conceded, mechanism rejected” is the common one, so a genre-savvy solver leans D. Note what has CHANGED: pre-repair the field was {C, D} on a shared opening clause; post-repair it is {A, D} on a shared concessive frame. Same size, different pair — see finding F2.
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.q2_lands_on: A for a solver who takes the contradictory-pair strip plus the absolutizer strip; open between two otherwise.
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.q2_path: Three strips, each independently attested. (1) B is a meta-claim about measurability and a non-answer to a ”Vad sägs i texten om X?” stem — G-STEM r2 performed this strip. (2) D is off-axis: three options concern payment, D concerns a sign. (3) A and C are DIRECT CONTRADICTORIES on the same quantity (nätter betalda / obetalda), and an item builder who plants a contradictory pair almost always keys inside it — so the field is {A, C}, i.e. 1-in-2, not the declared 1-in-3. A solver who then applies the standard absolutizer strip lands on A alone: C carries ”Nästan alla”, the set's only token from M-FORM's live _ABSOLUTIZERS list, and the bank's own RULE 13 teaches that the sweeping option is the distractor. Critically, the declared 1-in-3 derivation reaches its number by a channel the repair was built to CLOSE (inferring the column's direction from q1's option field), and it never considers the A/C pair at all.
blind_reconstruction_from_stems_sheet_on.empirical_counterweight: Recorded because it cuts against the reconstruction and must not be suppressed. G-STEM r2, holding both stems and both option sets and no passage, reported ”BLIND: PARTIALLY / pick C” on q:2 — it made strips (1) and (2), reached the A/C pair, and then chose the WRONG member of it, resolving on a cross-question stance inference that the repair had already weakened. So the chains above are heuristic, not deterministic, and the one live blind reader on record MISSED q2 rather than hitting it. On q:1 the same reader reported ”pick D” but explicitly called it ”a lean, not a decision”. That is why the floor findings are recorded at minor and note and why neither is a blocker.

q2_rounding_ruling.question: Is key A's ”Sju av tio nätter blev obetalda” an exam-fair rendering of ”en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna”?
q2_rounding_ruling.arithmetic: 31 % paid ⇒ 69 % unpaid. ”Sju av tio” = 70 %. Gap = 1 percentage point. Re-derived by this audit.
q2_rounding_ruling.case_against_fairness: The option is stated FLAT — ”blev obetalda” — with no ”ungefär”, ”drygt” or ”nära”, while the unit's own rationale hedges where the option does not (”alltså ungefär sju av tio obetalda”). A literal-minded solver who checks 69 ≠ 70 and expects an exactly-true option has nothing left to pick, since B, C and D are all plainly false. The unit therefore forces a choice with no arithmetically exact option in the set.
q2_rounding_ruling.case_for_fairness: Four grounds. (1) 69 % rounds to 70 % under any ordinary rule, and ”sju av tio” is an idiomatic Swedish rounded-proportion phrase, not a claim of exactness — the same phrase does duty across roughly 66–74 % in ordinary Swedish reporting. (2) No rival is closer: B denies a figure exists, D is unsupported, and C is on the opposite pole at ~90 %+ against A's 70 % — the discrimination the item actually asks for is pole plus magnitude, and A is unique on both. (3) The construct being tested is the COMPLEMENT FLIP (paid → unpaid), which the item performs correctly; the rounding is incidental to it and no distractor exploits it. (4) The HP contract on a ”Vad sägs i texten” item is best-supported-by-the-text, not arithmetically-exact, and authentic HP LÄS routinely keys rounded paraphrases of a passage figure.
q2_rounding_ruling.ruling: EXAM-FAIR. Recorded at note severity, no repair owed. The 1-pp gap is inside ordinary Swedish rounding for ”sju av tio”, the option is alone on the correct pole and magnitude, and the flip is the construct. Two hardenings exist if the owner wants the margin bought back, neither recommended: (i) change the passage figure 31 → 30, which makes ”sju av tio” exact but costs verisimilitude — 31 reads like a real follow-up figure, 30 reads like an authored one; or (ii) hedge the option to ”Ungefär sju av tio nätter blev obetalda”, which is worse, because it would make the KEY a hedged option in a question whose whole rule-10 design depends on the hedged option (B) being the WRONG one. Leave as is.

floors_assessment.q1_declared: 1-in-2 (NOTES §7, restated in §11 residue item 1; not present in generator_meta — see F13).
floors_assessment.q1_honest: NUMBER HONEST, DERIVATION FALSIFIED. 1-in-2 is the right number and it sits exactly at the policy line, not better than it. But §7's stated route — ”C and D are formally indistinguishable — both concede the need and reject the fee, differing only in who pays instead. Adversarial blind field = {C, D}” — describes the PRE-repair option C verbatim (”Utrustningen behövs, men föreningen bör bekosta den själv”). Post-repair C endorses the proposal and is a contrary of D, so that field no longer exists. The honest 1-in-2 now runs on a DIFFERENT pair: A and D are the two concessive two-part options, C is causal, B falls to scope. Field = {A, D}. §7 was never updated; §12 asserts the floor is ”improved, not merely restated” without correcting the derivation it points back to.
floors_assessment.q2_honest: OPTIMISTIC BY ONE STEP. Honest floor is 1-in-2, and a single survivor for a solver who also takes the absolutizer strip. The declared derivation fails twice: it reaches {A, B, D} by inferring the column's direction from q1's option field — the very cross-question channel fleet-repair-1 was built to close, so the derivation now argues against the repair's own success — and it never considers that A and C are direct contradictories on the payment rate, which is the strongest form channel in the set and the one both G-STEM rounds named. B is a non-answer to a ”Vad sägs i texten” stem and D is off-axis; {A, C} survives. 1-in-2 is still AT the tolerated ceiling, not above it, so the policy is not breached — but the declared number should read 1-in-2.
floors_assessment.ruling: FLOORS RULING: q1 = 1-in-2 (declared number correct, declared derivation falsified). q2 = 1-in-2 (declared 1-in-3 falsified; honest value one step worse). Both questions therefore sit EXACTLY at the 1-in-2 policy ceiling and neither sits above it. NOT BLOCKING. The unit is nonetheless materially stronger than its round-1 self: fleet-repair-1 removed a genuine containment defect (old C was a special case of key D, so D could not be uniquely correct) and gave the set a real pro-proposal position, which closed the stance-composition skew entirely — this unit now does BETTER than the owner ruling requires on composition, because an option asserting the position the author argues against is present.

stance_policy_compliance.policy: BRIEF-ADDENDUM efterhandstillägg 1 (ägardom batch16 dom 1): stance-composition skew in single-author opinion passages is WITHIN TOLERANCE and not a repairable structural leak; cross-question stance correlation is REPORTABLE at note severity and does not block, PROVIDED (a) the adversarial blind floor is stated explicitly and is no better than 1-in-2, and (b) rule 10 holds. G-STEM should continue to name it; adjudication should not treat it as an open major.
stance_policy_compliance.condition_a: MET, THINLY, AND WITH ONE CORRECTION. The floors are stated explicitly, twice (NOTES §7 and §11). q1's number is right at 1-in-2; q2's declared 1-in-3 is optimistic and the honest value is 1-in-2. Both honest values are AT the tolerated maximum rather than better than it, so the condition holds on the numbers that matter. What is refuted is the reasoning under both numbers, and the fact that the statement lives only in a NOTES file that does not travel with the unit (F13).
stance_policy_compliance.condition_b: HOLDS, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED. ”Pick the qualified/hedged option” is UNDECIDABLE on q1 (A ”kan godtas, men …” and D ”Utrustningen behövs, men …” share the concessive two-part shape) and selects a DISTRACTOR on q2 (the sole hedged option is B ”svår att mäta”, which is wrong; the key is flat and numeric). That is 0 to 0.5 of 2, inside rule 10's ≤ ½ bound. Rule 13's stricter form also holds: q1 has TWO qualified options rather than exactly one, and q2's single sweeping option (C, ”Nästan alla”) is a distractor facing an unabsolutized key — the required rule-10 break. Independently re-verified against the LIVE gate source: scanning all eight options against mech._ABSOLUTIZERS as imported in this worktree returns exactly one hit, q2-C on ”alla”; M-FORM passes because no question has an unabsolutized key facing three absolutized distractors.
stance_policy_compliance.ruling: COMPLIANT, RECORDED, NOT BLOCKING — consistent with the standing precedent in batches/batch16/audits/las-b16-002.json and batches/batch18/audits/las-b18-002.json. This audit is the adjudication step that converts the open G-STEM r2 q:2 major (which received no round-3 leg and carries no recorded disposition anywhere in batch19) into the note the owner ruling prescribes. The one cheap edit that would buy margin back, if wanted, does not touch the passage, the keys, the key letters or q1: re-cut q2-C so it is no longer the set's sole absolutizer — e.g. ”De flesta nätter blev betalda.” (5 words, ratio unchanged, same inversion trap, no new cross-question bridge, and it removes the strip that currently collapses the {A, C} pair to a single survivor).

findings.claim: q2's declared adversarial blind floor of 1-in-3 is optimistic by one step. The honest floor is 1-in-2, and a single survivor for a solver who also takes the absolutizer strip.
findings.evidence: NOTES §7 derives 1-in-3 as: ”A, B and D are all compatible with a critical column; C with a supportive one. A solver who has inferred the column's direction from q1's option field is left with three candidates.” Two objections, both from the bytes. (i) The mechanism it uses — inferring the direction from q1's option field — is the exact cross-question leak fleet-repair-1 was built to close, and §12 claims it closed (”q1's set no longer discloses the author's direction”). The derivation therefore argues against the repair's own recorded success. (ii) It never considers that A (”Sju av tio nätter blev obetalda”) and C (”Nästan alla nätter blev betalda”) are DIRECT CONTRADICTORIES on the same quantity, which is the strongest form channel in the set and which BOTH G-STEM rounds named at major severity (r1: ”A and C are contradictories on the payment rate, so the key is one of them and both D and B drop as off-axis”; r2: ”form alone leaves the A/C contradictory pair”). B is a meta-claim and a non-answer to a ”Vad sägs i texten om X?” stem; D concerns a sign rather than payment. Field = {A, C} = 1-in-2. C additionally carries ”Nästan alla”, the set's only live M-FORM absolutizer token, which the bank's own RULE 13 teaches solvers to strip.
findings.why: Non-blocking. 1-in-2 is AT the stance policy's tolerated ceiling, not above it, so condition (a) still holds and the item is still inside the rules. But the declared number is what the policy's compliance rests on and it should read 1-in-2. Counterweight recorded and not suppressed: G-STEM r2's live blind reader reached the {A, C} pair and then picked C — the wrong member — so the chain is heuristic, not deterministic.

findings.stage_challenged: blind floors / self-blind-solve (q1) — derivation, not number

Adversarial blind field = {C, D}.” That is a description of the PRE-repair C, ”Utrustningen behövs, men föreningen bör bekosta den själv”. The shipping C is ”Förslaget bör genomföras som det ligger, eftersom badgästerna har nytta av utrustningen” — it neither concedes the need nor rejects the fee, and it is a contrary of D rather than its twin. §7's with-passage paragraph is stale in the same way: it refutes C by pointing at the driftsbudget sentence and the association's payment for tillsyn, which is the refutation of the OLD C; the new C needs the retraction plus the geography defeat of the benefit principle, which the unit's own shipping rationale does correctly supply. Re-derived from the stems sheet: B falls to scope, and the two concessive two-part options are now A (”kan godtas, men …”) and D (”Utrustningen behövs, men …”) against causal C and conditional B, so the honest field is {A, D} — same size, different pair.
findings.why: Non-blocking, and the underlying repair was a genuine improvement: old C was a special case of key D, so D could not be uniquely correct, and that defect is fully closed. The record simply was not brought forward. §12 asserts the floor is ”improved, not merely restated” while leaving the derivation it points back to describing deleted bytes.

findings.stage_challenged: repair_log claim / hedge balance (fleet-repair-1, q1 option C)

The consequence is visible in NOTES §5, whose hedge table still records ”A (’kan godtas, men …’) and C (’Utrustningen behövs, men …’) share the same qualified two-part shape; C is a deliberate formal twin of the key” — post-repair the key's formal twin is A, and the qualified count is two (A, D), not three. findings.stage_challenged: naming registry / RULE 8-9 near-duplicate (NEW — found by this audit, missed by every gate)
findings.claim: The coined toponym stem ”Vässling-” grazes an already-shipped invented Swedish municipality in the same lane. batch15's las-b15-002 runs on ”Vässlinge”; this unit coins ”Vässlingsbadet” and logs ”Vässlingen”.
findings.evidence: batches/batch15/candidates-final/las-b15-002.json, family foreningslokaler-halltider-debatt-short — the SAME debatt-short lane — carries ”Vässlinge” five times: title ”Tisdagskvällar i Vässlinges gymnastiksalar”, ”Den som ringer fritidskontoret i Vässlinge”, ”ordförande i Vässlinge gymnastikförening”, and twice in its own originality_note, which registers it explicitly as ”den påhittade kommunen Vässlinge”. ”Vässlingen” is exactly ONE letter from ”Vässlinge”, and ”Vässlingsbadet” is that stem plus -s-badet. Neither the generator nor G-REGISTER could have caught it honestly: the BRIEF-ADDENDUM's excluded-toponym registry (Myrsjövägen, Tunbergsvägen, Vrantebo, Hyllemåla, Rossmåla, Sölvinge, Flarkbro, Brantmyr-, Näversved-, Bjässemon, Klyvinge, Härkilsnäs, Ylmaren, Stintbury) OMITS Vässlinge, and G-REGISTER checked this unit's toponyms against that list by name and cleared them. The defect is in the registry; the consequence lands here.
findings.why: Not a law-16 matter — there is no real bearer of either name — and not a blocker: the bank already carries the Quennerly/Quennerby near-pair under disposition, so a near-pair has shipped before. But BRIEF-ADDENDUM's RULE 8 addition says in terms ”do not add more”, and RULE 14 extends one-letter-variant probing to toponyms. The fix is unusually cheap and is an OWNER call, not this audit's: ”Vässlingsbadet” occurs exactly twice in the shipping bytes (the title and one passage word, ”Vid Vässlingsbadet hänger en livboj”), ”Vässlingen” occurs ZERO times outside the search log, and no key, rationale, option or stem contains either. A rename off the Vässling- stem costs two tokens plus the originality_note. The separate and more durable action is to add Vässlinge to the excluded-toponym registry so the next batch is not exposed to the same blind spot.

findings.claim: Three law-16 probes the generator's log did not run, all closed by this audit. None is a collision, but one returns real bearers and one methodological trap deserves recording.

R. Odgren (co-author on a 2004 genetics paper), and the Lincoln-Sudbury Regional High School article. (ii) The real Swedish surname ÖGREN (2 134 bearers, national rank 443) and Öhgren (317) sit one insertion from ”Ödgren”; ”Ödgren” itself returns no bearer count anywhere. (iii) WIKIDATA added as a third index: control ”Flarken” returns 8 entities, all four coined names return 0.

The hazard RULE 14 names is a coined name landing on a real MAP FEATURE (”real ’Rössmåla’ sits one diacritic from batch16's ’Rossmåla’”); a Swedish surname sharing a stem with unrelated American bearers of an unaccented spelling is not that hazard, and is unavoidable in any invented Swedish surname — proximity to Ögren is precisely what makes the coinage read native. The full pair ”Bengta Ödgren” is zero on five indexes. METHODOLOGICAL WARNING for future auditors, verified in this session: namntips.se auto-generates a statistics page for ANY surname string — its ”Ödgren” page exists and lists the national top-200 given names with NO bearer count, whereas its ”Ögren” page reports 2 134. The existence of such a page is not evidence of bearers and must not be read as a hit.
